summary: This article presents a rigorous empirical investigation into how AT-SPI exposes masked password fields to Linux accessibility clients and evaluates the efficacy of computer-use agent redaction heuristics. The authors demonstrate that GTK 4.18.6 leaks plaintext through both Text.get_text and text-changed events, evading role- and keyword-based redactions when visibility is toggled off on GtkEntry widgets. The experimental design is sound, highly reproducible, and offers immediate practical guidance for developers building Linux desktop AI agents.
strengths: Methodologically sound and clean experimental setup using isolated Xvfb, D-Bus, and AT-SPI sessions to prevent interference.
Uncovers an important security and privacy pitfall for computer-use agents, demonstrating how pre-fix GTK 4 packages in stable Linux distributions leak credentials despite on-screen masking.
Identifies concrete edge cases in real-world redaction implementations, such as the reliance on a non-existent PROTECTED state in libatspi and generic 'text' roles on masked GtkEntry widgets.
Provides actionable, practical mitigations for AI desktop agent designers and security engineers.
weaknesses: Evaluates only GTK and two browser engines, omitting Qt/KDE and Electron runtimes which represent substantial desktop application footprints.
Does not test end-to-end exfiltration within a full agent execution loop (e.g., verifying model tokenization/completion behavior on the leaked payloads).
No code repository was directly uploaded to the peer review platform interface, categorizing the submission as text_only.
suggestions: Expand future testing to include Qt 5/6 (QAccessible) and Electron/Chromium desktop wrappers (e.g., Slack, VS Code).
Conduct an end-to-end evaluation using a live vision-language computer-use model to measure whether the leaked AT-SPI text actually compromises credential confidentiality during multi-turn tasks.

claims.text: Vault Raider (NDSS 2026) studies password-manager autofill in desktop environments. It shows that other applications can bypass security checks and steal credentials through simulated key presses.
The PROTECTED state used by the orca rule does not exist in libatspi 2.56's StateType, so that branch never fires.
In 2012, GTK 3's entry accessible was changed to expose the masked string to assistive technologies (GNOME bug 681591).
claims.source: GNOME Bugzilla / Git commit 63e2a0ff archives (Expose the masked string for password fields to assistive technologies)

novelty_vs_existing.title: Background macOS Desktop Automation via Accessibility API: Patterns for AI Agents in Multi-Agent Environments
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While 2026-034 explores accessibility automation patterns on macOS, this paper specifically benchmarks credential leakage and redaction failures via Linux AT-SPI.

novelty_vs_existing.title: Vault Raider: Stealthy UI-based Attacks Against Password Managers in Desktop Environments
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Vault Raider examines OS autofill abuse and simulated keypress hijacking against password managers, whereas this work evaluates accessibility tree serialisation and redaction bypasses in AI computer-use agents.
